profile.what: Goldman Sachs is the leading global investment bank, advising on mergers, underwriting stock and bond issues, trading for institutional clients, and managing assets and wealth for wealthy individuals and institutions.
profile.money: Fees from advising on deals and underwriting, trading revenue from making markets in stocks, bonds and commodities for hedge funds and institutions, and asset- and wealth-management fees. Revenue swings with deal activity and market volatility; it has largely exited consumer banking.
profile.valued: Investment banks are valued on price to book and P/E. Goldman's multiple rises when deal-making recovers and when the steadier asset- and wealth-management business grows as a share of earnings.
profile.peer_group: Financials · bank, insurer or asset manager

valuation.method: Banks are valued on book value, not free cash flow. Justified price-to-book = (ROE − 3% growth) ÷ (required return − 3%), using a normalised ROE of 12.0% (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM, capped at 25%) and a required return of 11% (low) to 9% (high): 1.12–1.50 × book value per share of $418.56.

methods.name: Excess-return model on book value
methods.basis: Book value per share $418.56 × 1.12–1.50. This is how Damodaran values banks and insurers: equity is worth book value plus the returns earned above the cost of equity.
